title: Thresholded throughput certifier and smoothing autoscaler
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: As Dedicated customers require predictable throughput guarantees while avoiding excessive overprovisioning, we need a controller that issues soft throughput certificates per-tenant and uses a damped autoscaling loop to smooth provisioning during transient spikes. This PR introduces a Thresholded Throughput Certifier (TTC) and a Smoothing Autoscaler that consume utilization and token-bucket style signals to certify short-term throughput guarantees and drive scale decisions. Motivation: Prior reactive autoscalers caused sharp up/down churn and noisy billing for tenants with bursty but bounded traffic. TTC establishes an explicit, decaying 'certified throughput' envelope based on recent high-percentile delivery and a configurable safety margin. The Smoothing Autoscaler uses the envelope to prefer gradual upscales, limited fast ramps for confirmed certificate breaches, and conservative downscales with a deploy-time hysteresis. Summary of changes: 1) telemetry/throughput_certifier.go: new certifier that computes sliding-window p95/p99 throughput, applies configurable thresholds, issues TTL-bound certificates, and emits metrics: ttc_cert_issued, ttc_cert_expired, ttc_cert_utilization_ratio. 2) autoscaler/smoother_controller.go: new controller that ingests certificates, utilization histograms, and queue-length signals; implements damped rate-of-change limiting, emergency ramp path (for sustained 30s breaches), and soft-fallback to lower-cost model variants when cold-starts risk SLOs. 3) api/throughput_cert_crd.yaml: CRD schema for ThroughputCertificate objects (versioned v1alpha1). 4) docs/operations/throughput-certifier.md: operator playbook for tuning margin, TTL, and emergency ramps. 5) tests/smoother_unit_test.go and e2e/scale_scenarios.yaml: unit and end-to-end scenarios covering synthetic microbursts, steady increases, and noise robustness. 6) examples/private/tenant-cert-example.yaml: example tenant config showing certificate goals and conservative-downscale flags. Commits: "init: add throughput certifier prototype and CRD","autoscaler: integrate smoother controller and emergency ramp path","telemetry: wire metrics and unit tests","docs: add operator playbook and examples","tests: add e2e scenarios and CI gating" Files changed (high level): - pkg/autoscaler/smoother_controller.go: core logic (~420 LOC) with comments and exported tuning knobs - pkg/telemetry/throughput_certifier.go: calculation and metrics (~180 LOC) - api/throughput_cert_crd.yaml: CRD and validation schema - docs/operations/throughput-certifier.md: ops playbook and tuning guide - tests/smoother_unit_test.go: 9 unit tests - e2e/scale_scenarios.yaml: three workload profiles Highlights and rationale: - Certificate model: compute sliding-window 5m p95 and 1m p99 delivery rates, then apply a margin multiplier (default 0.85) and an exponential decay with configurable half-life to produce a TTL-bound certificate. Certificates are advisory but surfaced to autoscaler and Console. - Autoscaler behavior: default is conservative smoothing (max 10% scale-up per minute, max 5% scale-down per minute). If certificate breaches are sustained beyond emergencyWindow (30s by default), an emergency ramp can increase capacity up to a configured fastRampPct. - Cost controls: when emergency ramp triggers, system prefers cheaper model variants (quantized) for newly provisioned capacity; this is opt-in per-tenant. - Observability: added tracing spans for cert issuance and scale decisions; Console dashboard tiles baked into docs. Backwards compatibility: the CRD is opt-in; default behavior when TTC is not present remains unchanged. Tests: unit tests verify certificate math, TTL decay, and controller damping. E2E scenarios run against local canary cluster and assert bounded churn and sustained SLOs for synthetic tenants. Review summary and conversation: "Arjun Patel requested more fine-grained metrics and explicit labels on certificate objects for tenant-scoped aggregation; noted potential race between CRD reconciliation and autoscaler informer cache." "Author (Maya Chen) replied: added ttc_cert_tenant and ttc_request_scope labels, and increased informer resync in controller; added comment and test to demonstrate reconciliation order resilience." "Leila Gomez asked for hard limits to prevent runaway emergency ramps; author responded by adding a global emergencyBudget and test coverage for budget exhaustion behavior." "Tomás requested clearer operator guidance on margin selection; docs updated with sample SLI-to-margin mapping and a tuning checklist." CI and validation: initial CI run had a flaky e2e failure in scale_scenarios (test flaked under 1% variance); reran with e2e test stabilization patch and all checks passed. CI checks: unit tests (pass), linters (pass), build (pass), e2e (pass). Security review: quick pass for CRD validation schema and RBAC rules; no privileged access added. Merge notes: squashed and merged to main after approvals from Arjun and Leila. Merge method: squash. Merge commit: "squash! Thresholded throughput certifier and smoothing autoscaler (Maya Chen)" Rollout plan and ops notes: - Begin as opt-in per-tenant by applying ThroughputCertificate objects. - Monitor metrics: ttc_cert_issued, ttc_cert_utilization_ratio, autoscaler_smooth_scale_events. - Start with conservative margin (0.7-0.85) and longer TTL (default 10m) for first 2 weeks. - Track billing deltas and adjust emergencyBudget to cap rapid cost spikes. Release notes: "Introduce Thresholded Throughput Certifier (TTC) and Smoothing Autoscaler to provide advisory short-term throughput guarantees and reduce autoscaling churn. TTC is opt-in via CRD. Adds new metrics and operator guidance for tuning." Breaking change: false
